blocks.text: add-block-type — the flagship — a PortableDoc block on every surface

content.value: The chore this replaces is the worst one Barkpark has: a new block type means a Go renderer, its named test, a DefaultRegistry entry, a JS emitter plus its coreEmitters map entry, a CASES fixture plus a count bump, and an Elixir compose_block clause that must land

the unknown-type catch-all at compose.ex:1190 — clause order is load-bearing. The command does all of it: two files created, six injections across four files, every anchor grep-proven unique. The JS surface is fail-closed at four edits — the react suite asserts CASES ≡ REGISTERED_TYPES and pins the exact count, so an emitter alone reds exactly one assertion; the count crosses as a declared CountBefore/CountAfter pair because Scaffy has no arithmetic. And it is honest about its edges: composition tier, walk.ex kinds, and CSS are documented conditional steps, never blind ops — the claim is 3 required code surfaces with test parity at birth, not "4 surfaces auto-injected".

So giving a plugin a new verb is appending one data map to its

The append REPLACEs the list's final ticket.close map (unique: grep count 1) with itself plus the new map, guarded by the new map's own id: line. # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Why this command is a ONE-LINE append (the architecture already did the work)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# There is NO handler key to write. `bp` is manifest-driven: the Go binary
# (internal/cli) has zero per-command code. It reads GET /v1/capabilities, walks
# the noun/verb tree (tree.Lookup), and builds the HTTP call GENERICALLY from the
# command map's own fields — `internal/cli/cli.go:9` composes the request from
# `http.path_template` via `manifest.BuildURL`, and `internal/cli/run.go:130`
# takes the method straight from `cmd.HTTP.Method`. No switch, no registration,
# no recompile.
#
# The round-trip, end to end:
#
#     cli_commands/0 list entry            (this append — the ONLY edit)
#        │  Plugins.Tickets.cli_commands/0 delegates to Tickets.CLI.commands/0
#        ▼
#     GET /v1/capabilities                 (the capabilities fold stamps every
#        │                                   plugin map with provenance: the
#        │                                   OWNING PLUGIN's registered name,
#        │                                   looked up noun→plugin — here
#        │                                   source: "plugin:tickets". The noun
#        │                                   is the lookup KEY, never the value:
#        │                                   capabilities.ex:200-213; doctrine
#        │                                   plugin.ex:506-508)
#        ▼
#     bp <noun> <verb>                     (tree.Lookup finds the map; the
#                                           generic HTTP builder calls
#                                           http.method + http.path_template)
#
# So: append the map here, and `bp ticket <verb>` works on the next capabilities
# fetch. No Go file is touched by this command — that is the whole point.
#
# Exemplar payload: the `ticket.inbox` map, api/lib/barkpark/plugins/tickets/cli.ex:87-104
# — the canonical read-list verb shape (id / noun / verb / summary /
# http{method,path_template} / auth_tier / args / flags / writes / batch /
# paginated / dry_run / default_output / scoped_prefix). This command templates
# that exact archetype: a read-tier GET list verb with a `limit` flag. For a
# WRITING verb, flip `method`/`writes`/`auth_tier`/`default_output` by hand — the
# map SHAPE is identical, only these four values change.
#
# Optional cosmetic polish (NOT part of this command, never a MARK): if the new
# verb returns a single wrapped object and you want its fields rendered as
# key/value lines instead of a one-row table, add the envelope key to
# `singleObjectEnvelopeKeys` at internal/cli/table.go:96. That is a Go rendering
# nicety only; the verb is fully functional without it.

# Token spellings-as-transforms (D3d / A1). A verb is a single lowercase word, so
# only the lowercase casings coincide (Pascal and SCREAMING differ) — declared for grammar completeness:
#   {{.Verb}}   → Stats     (Pascal)
#   {{.verb}}   → stats     (kebab == camel == snake, lowercase)

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# OP — append the new verb map to the ticket noun's command list (A3)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The list `ticket_commands/0` ends with the `ticket.close` map, whose closing
# `}` carries NO trailing comma before the `]` (verified: cli.ex:149-166). Under
# A3 you cannot bare-INSERT a second map after it — two adjacent `%{…} %{…}` terms
# are a syntax error. The append is therefore a FENCED REPLACE of that last
# element: re-emit `ticket.close` verbatim, add the separating comma, then the new
# map. The `ticket.close` target is unique (`grep -c 'id: "ticket.close"'` = 1).
#
# A4/A5 guard: `ticket.close` survives as a substring of the replacement, so
# idempotency rests ENTIRELY on the ASLONG guard — a payload-derived, ASCII,
# per-verb substring of what the op writes (the new map's `id:` line — chosen over
# the mark line because it ALSO refuses a verb that already exists by hand). No

# Prior art: `mix ecto.gen.migration <name>` already stamps an empty timestamped
# skeleton — this command formalizes that same convention, then fills the body
# with the shape we actually reach for (alter + add + partial backfill index),
# modeled 1:1 on api/priv/repo/migrations/20260714150200_add_chat_execution_event_projection.exs.
#
# CREATE-only by design: migrations are never edited in place and never registered
# anywhere — the migrator discovers them by the {{.Ts}} filename prefix. There is
# no accretion file to inject into, so this command has zero IN ops.
#
# IDEMPOTENCY WARNING — the guard is the FILENAME, and Ts is part of it. IF
# ABSENT makes a re-run with the SAME Ts a no-op, but a re-run with a FRESH Ts
# and identical remaining args creates a second, differently-named migration
# with a duplicate body: the second `alter table ... add` of the same column
# fails when the migrator applies it. A fresh Ts is a NEW migration, never a
# retry — to re-run this command, reuse the original Ts.
CREATE FILE IF ABSENT "api/priv/repo/migrations/{{.Ts}}_{{.migration_name}}.exs"
WITH
::: {{.migration-name}} migration :::
defmodule Barkpark.Repo.Migrations.{{.MigrationName}} do
  use Ecto.Migration

  def change do
    alter table(:{{.table_name}}) do
      add :{{.column_name}}, {{.column_type}}
    end

    # Partial index, mirroring the exemplar's backfill shape: indexes only the rows
    # still awaiting a value. Narrow the predicate to the real invariant this column
    # guards, or drop `where:` for a plain index. `change/0` auto-reverses all three
    # ops (alter/add + create index), so `mix ecto.rollback` needs no `down/0`.
    create index(:{{.table_name}}, [:{{.column_name}}], where: "{{.column_name}} IS NULL")
  end
end
::: {{.migration-name}} migration :::

# ASSERT FILE guards are ASCII, brace-safe (every `}}` is followed by a space, `)`, `,`
# or `]`, never a literal `}`), and each is a verbatim substring of the payload above.
ASSERT FILE "api/priv/repo/migrations/{{.Ts}}_{{.migration_name}}.exs" CONTAINS "defmodule Barkpark.Repo.Migrations.{{.MigrationName}} do"
ASSERT FILE "api/priv/repo/migrations/{{.Ts}}_{{.migration_name}}.exs" CONTAINS "alter table(:{{.table_name}}) do"
ASSERT FILE "api/priv/repo/migrations/{{.Ts}}_{{.migration_name}}.exs" CONTAINS "add :{{.column_name}}, {{.column_type}}"
ASSERT FILE "api/priv/repo/migrations/{{.Ts}}_{{.migration_name}}.exs" CONTAINS "create index(:{{.table_name}}, [:{{.column_name}}]"

# ===========================================================================
# add-plugin — the DECLARATIVE form of `mix barkpark.plugin.new <name>`.
#
# PRIOR ART. Today a plugin skeleton is scaffolded imperatively by the Mix
# task `mix barkpark.plugin.new <name>` (api/lib/mix/tasks/barkpark.plugin.new.ex),
# which renders four EEx templates under api/priv/templates/plugin_new/. This
# command formalizes that generator into a single reversible .scaffy document,
# mirroring those templates VERBATIM (their EEx interpolations become declared
# VARIABLEs). The older `mix barkpark.gen.plugin` is DEPRECATED and merely
# delegates to `barkpark.plugin.new` (barkpark.gen.plugin.ex:11-12); the
# similarly-named `mix barkpark.plugin.gen_types` is a DIFFERENT domain
# (it regenerates priv/plugin_types.d.ts from the manifest JSON Schema) and
# does not collide with this command.
#
# ALL-CREATE, ZERO INJECTION. Unlike add-block-type or add-oban-worker, this
# command touches NO accretion file — there is no registry, router, barrel, or
# config map to inject into. The annotated file tree is therefore all-● (five
# created files, zero ○ injected rows). The reason is architectural, not an
# oversight:
#
#   * DISCOVERY IS AUTOMATIC. `Barkpark.Plugins.Registry.Discovery` walks
#     priv/plugins/*/plugin.json at boot (plugin_dirs_in/1, read in
#     registry/boot_collectors.ex:140-142) and registers every manifest it
#     finds. The boot invocation is `Barkpark.Plugins.Registry.discover_and_register()`
#     at schema_bootstrap.ex:62 — SchemaBootstrap is a supervised child
#     (application.ex:192), started after the Registry GenServer and before
#     Oban; registry.ex:366-367 is only a defdelegate to the implementation,
#     `Discovery.discover_and_register/0` (discovery.ex:52). Dropping
#     a plugin.json under priv/plugins/ IS the registration. The
#     `config :barkpark, :plugins` list is NOT a registry: unset ⇒ discover
#     everything; set ⇒ it acts only as a kill-switch / whitelist of
#     plugin_names (registry.ex:13, :33). A minimal plugin needs no config
#     edit, so this command plants none.
#
#   * NO MIGRATION. A plugin ships no migration. Schemas declared by a plugin's
#     `register_schemas/1` callback are UPSERTED into the host's generic tables
#     at boot by `Barkpark.Plugins.Bootstrap.register_all_schemas/0`
#     (bootstrap.ex:61) — idempotent on (name, dataset). Plugin data rides the
#     host schema; there are no plugin-owned tables to create.
#
# Because every op below is a whole-file CREATE FILE IF ABSENT, idempotency and
# reversibility are structural: IF ABSENT is the guard (a second run writes
# nothing), and the created file paths are the remove handles (Wave-3 `remove`
# deletes exactly this set, leaving the tree byte-clean). No in-file MARK is
# needed — MARK anchors a marker INSIDE a host file, and this command has no
# host file. Hand-apply check (D7): the output is byte-identical to
# `mix barkpark.plugin.new {{.plugin_name}}` run with no --capabilities.
# ===========================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1/5 ● Manifest — priv/plugins/<name>/plugin.json
#     Mirrors plugin.json.eex. Discovery reads this file; `module` must match
#     the entry module so Registry.resolve_module/1 agrees. Minimal plugin
#     declares no capabilities (empty list, exactly as the generator emits
#     with no --capabilities flag).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE FILE IF ABSENT "api/priv/plugins/{{.plugin_name}}/plugin.json"
WITH
::: {{.plugin_name}} manifest :::
{
  "plugin_name": "{{.plugin_name}}",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "description": "{{.Description}}",
  "capabilities": [],
  "module": "Barkpark.Plugins.{{.PluginName}}"
}
::: {{.plugin_name}} manifest :::

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2/5 ● Entry module — lib/barkpark/plugins/<name>.ex
#     Mirrors lib/plugin.ex.eex. ONE line of body: `use Barkpark.Plugin`. The
#     behaviour reads + validates the manifest at COMPILE time (no runtime
#     eval). Lives in the compiled tree (elixirc_paths sees it) so the plugin
#     actually registers. manifest_path climbs three dirs from
#     lib/barkpark/plugins/ to the app root, then down into priv/plugins/.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE FILE IF ABSENT "api/lib/barkpark/plugins/{{.plugin_name}}.ex"
WITH
::: {{.plugin_name}} entry module :::
defmodule Barkpark.Plugins.{{.PluginName}} do
  @moduledoc """
  {{.Description}}

  Generated by `mix barkpark.plugin.new {{.plugin_name}}`.

  Capabilities: (none)

  This module lives in the compiled tree at
  `lib/barkpark/plugins/{{.plugin_name}}.ex` so it is reachable by
  `elixirc_paths` and registers via `Barkpark.Plugins.Registry`. The
  manifest at `priv/plugins/{{.plugin_name}}/plugin.json` is read +
  validated at compile time by `Barkpark.Plugin.__using__/1` (D7 — no
  runtime eval), and its `"module"` key points back at this module so
  discovery matches.

  Drop schemas into `priv/plugins/{{.plugin_name}}/schemas/` and add any
  custom logic below.
  """

  use Barkpark.Plugin, manifest_path: "../../../priv/plugins/{{.plugin_name}}/plugin.json"
end
::: {{.plugin_name}} entry module :::

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3/5 ● README — priv/plugins/<name>/README.md
#     Mirrors README.md.eex. The Capabilities section renders empty for a
#     minimal (zero-capability) plugin — byte-identical to the generator.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE FILE IF ABSENT "api/priv/plugins/{{.plugin_name}}/README.md"
WITH
::: {{.plugin_name}} readme :::
# {{.plugin_name}}

{{.Description}}

## Capabilities



## Layout

The entry module lives in the compiled tree so it actually registers; the
manifest, schemas, and this README live under `priv/plugins/{{.plugin_name}}/`.

```
lib/barkpark/plugins/{{.plugin_name}}.ex     # plugin module (use Barkpark.Plugin)
test/barkpark/plugins/{{.plugin_name}}_test.exs  # on the mix test path
priv/plugins/{{.plugin_name}}/
├── plugin.json                   # manifest (validated at compile time)
├── README.md                     # this file
└── schemas/                      # plugin schema definitions
```

## Adding code

- Schemas: drop JSON or Elixir schema files into
  `priv/plugins/{{.plugin_name}}/schemas/`.
- Logic: extend the module in `lib/barkpark/plugins/{{.plugin_name}}.ex`.
- Tests: add cases to `test/barkpark/plugins/{{.plugin_name}}_test.exs`
  and run `mix test`.

## Verifying

```bash
cd api
mix compile
mix test test/barkpark/plugins/{{.plugin_name}}_test.exs
```

- `docs/plugins/SCHEMA_V2.md` — composite, arrayOf, codelist, localizedText
- `Barkpark.Plugin` behaviour — `lib/barkpark/plugin.ex`
- `Barkpark.Plugins.Registry` — discovery & registration entrypoint
::: {{.plugin_name}} readme :::

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4/5 ● Schemas dir keeper — priv/plugins/<name>/schemas/.gitkeep
#     The generator writes an empty .gitkeep so the (initially empty) schemas
#     directory is tracked. Drop schema definitions here later.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE FILE IF ABSENT "api/priv/plugins/{{.plugin_name}}/schemas/.gitkeep"
WITH
::: {{.plugin_name}} gitkeep :::
::: {{.plugin_name}} gitkeep :::

# 5/5 ● Manifest test — test/barkpark/plugins/<name>_test.exs
#     Mirrors test/plugin_test.exs.eex. Proves the entry module parses its
#     manifest. Lives on the `mix test` path so CI exercises it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE FILE IF ABSENT "api/test/barkpark/plugins/{{.plugin_name}}_test.exs"
WITH
::: {{.plugin_name}} test :::
defmodule Barkpark.Plugins.{{.PluginName}}Test do
  use ExUnit.Case, async: true

  test "manifest/0 returns the parsed plugin.json map" do
    manifest = Barkpark.Plugins.{{.PluginName}}.manifest()

    assert is_map(manifest)
    assert manifest["plugin_name"] == "{{.plugin_name}}"
    assert manifest["version"] == "0.1.0"
    assert is_list(manifest["capabilities"])
  end
end
::: {{.plugin_name}} test :::

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# What this command does (and, deliberately, does NOT touch)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A new public v1 error code is a SMALL, CLOSED edit surface — the query/legacy
# "duplicated error emitters" scar is healed: 13 controllers action_fallback into
# FallbackController → Content.Errors, so both controllers emit only shared
# tuples (charter D54a). There is NO FOREACH-over-emitters to do. The mechanizable
# surface is exactly THREE sites, all in two files:
#
#   ● errors.ex @hints  — the fix-suggesting hint, keyed off the stable `code`.
#                         Registering it here is what enters the code into
#                         known_codes/0 (errors.ex:132-134 = Map.keys(@hints) ∪
#                         @public_inline_codes), and THAT is the single source
#                         for the served OpenAPI `Error.code` enum. (Op A)
#   ● errors.ex build/1 — the clause that maps {:error, :code} to the
#                         {code, message, status} envelope, inserted BEFORE the
#                         true catch-all (which matches everything). (Op B)
#   ● errors_test.exs   — a unit test pinning the envelope shape AND the
#                         known_codes/0 membership (the DELIBERATE tripwire —
#                         known_codes derives from @hints, so the OpenAPI
#                         drift-guard is a tautology; only a membership test
#                         catches a dropped @hints entry). (Op C)
#
# TWO ACCRETION IDIOMS, chosen by the SEPARATOR of the collection each op grows:
#   • Op A grows the @hints MAP, whose entries are COMMA-separated. Its last
#     entry (quota_exceeded) carries no trailing comma before the closing `}`, so
#     a bare INSERT would abut two map pairs with no separator (a syntax error).
#     The fix is the A3 comma-list idiom: a self-consuming REPLACE that re-emits
#     the last entry WITH a comma + the new entry, guarded by a payload-derived
#     ASLONG and REANCHOR (E-005). REANCHOR's splice inserts a COMMA between
#     siblings — exactly right for a map. The map's `}` is OUTSIDE the anchor.
#   • Ops B and C grow collections of `defp` clauses / `test` blocks, which are
#     separated by BLANK LINES, not commas. REANCHOR would wrongly splice a comma
#     between them (a syntax error), so they use INSERT AFTER FIRST instead: the
#     new block is inserted after a fixed, stable anchor and the anchor is left
#     intact (never self-consuming, so E-005 does not apply). Idempotency is the
#     engine's implicit planted-MARK guard — a second run with the same code sees
#     its own `MARK:error-…-<code>` already present and skips. Sibling accretion
#     is LIFO (each new code lands right after the same anchor), which is fine:
#     order among these blocks is irrelevant (disjoint clause patterns; a flat
#     test list).
#
# SELF-DERIVING — ZERO ops, do NOT touch:
#   • known_codes/0 (errors.ex:132-134) recomputes from @hints on every call.
#   • The OpenAPI `Error.code` enum (Barkpark.Api.OpenApi) reads known_codes/0.
#   • test/barkpark_web/contract/error_code_coverage_test.exs globs the controller
#     dirs for emitted codes and asserts emitted ⊆ known_codes — a build/1-only
#     code (never written INLINE by a controller) simply never appears in
#     `emitted`, so growing known_codes can never red it.
#
# NOT MECHANIZED — one required MANUAL step (see the §9 note at the bottom):
#   • docs/api-v1.md §9 is a HAND-CURATED human prose list, and it IS gate-locked
#     by errors_doc_coverage_test.exs (every known code must appear verbatim in
#     backticks in §9). A generic command cannot mechanize the append: (1) §9 is
#     editorial prose grouped by category (core / additive / endpoint-specific) —
#     which bucket a new code belongs to is a human judgment; (2) api-v1.md sits
#     at its CI-enforced byte budget (13991/14000 B — 9 bytes of headroom), so a
#     mechanical append overflows check-doc-budgets.sh, and the doc contract
#     FORBIDS raising the cap. Adding the §9 line (with a compensating prose
#     trim) is the author's one hand-edit; this command is loud about it rather
#     than papering over it or falsely claiming self-derivation.

# Token spellings-as-transforms (D3d / A1). error_code is OPAQUE (its VALUE is
# substituted verbatim, never re-cased). Under D22 an OPAQUE reference uses ONE
# spelling per file — any legal joiner-output of the declared name. This file uses
# the kebab spelling {{.error-code}} throughout, because a MARK name must be kebab
# (E-019) and the snake `error_code` would red it. The value is unaffected:
#   {{.error-code}}  → playground_expired  (the --var value, verbatim)

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# OP A — register the fix-suggesting hint (this is what enters known_codes/0)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The @hints map's LAST entry is `"quota_exceeded" => "…"` (errors.ex:72-73) and
# the map's closing `}` (:74) follows with NO trailing comma before it — a bare
# INSERT of a second entry abuts two map pairs with no separator (Elixir syntax
# error). Under A3 the append is a FENCED REPLACE of that last ENTRY (the `}` stays
# OUTSIDE the anchor, exactly like add-oban-worker keeps the `]` outside): re-emit
# the quota_exceeded entry WITH a trailing comma, then the mark comment, then the
# new `"{{.error-code}}" => "{{.Hint}}"` entry.
#
# A4/A5 + E-005: the quota_exceeded entry survives as a substring of the
# replacement (self-consuming), so idempotency rests on the payload-derived
# ASLONG guard (the per-code mark substring — ASCII, brace-safe, and it ALSO
# refuses a code already hand-registered under the same mark). REANCHOR makes the
# sibling-accretion path first-class: the first code anchors on the quota_exceeded
# structural target and plants MARK:error-hint-<code>; a later code anchors at the
# LAST planted mark block of that family (the mark comment + its entry line, whose
# tail ends in `"`) and WITH re-emits that block + comma + the new entry — the map
# grows at the family's tail, the structural target is never re-matched once
# consumed, and same-code re-runs are a no-op.
IN "api/lib/barkpark/content/errors.ex"
### Append {{.error-code}} hint to the @hints map after the quota_exceeded entry
REPLACE
::: quota_exceeded hint entry :::
    "quota_exceeded" =>
      "This workspace has reached its write quota (details.quota). Remove documents to free capacity, or raise the workspace's quota."
::: quota_exceeded hint entry :::
WITH
::: quota_exceeded plus {{.error-code}} hint :::
    "quota_exceeded" =>
      "This workspace has reached its write quota (details.quota). Remove documents to free capacity, or raise the workspace's quota.",
    # scaffy:add-error-shape {{.error-code}} MARK:error-hint-{{.error-code}}
    "{{.error-code}}" => "{{.Hint}}"
::: quota_exceeded plus {{.error-code}} hint :::
MARK "error-hint-{{.error-code}}"
REANCHOR "error-hint-"
ASLONG FILE DONT CONTAIN "MARK:error-hint-{{.error-code}}"

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# OP B — the build/1 clause, inserted BEFORE the true catch-all
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The catch-all `defp build(_)` (errors.ex:498-499) maps ANY unrecognized reason
# to a 500, so a new clause MUST precede it. `defp` clauses are separated by BLANK
# LINES, not commas, so this is an INSERT AFTER FIRST (not the A3 comma idiom): the
# anchor is the last real clause before the catch-all — the is_binary/internal_error
# clause (:495-496, unique) — and the new clause is inserted right after it, still
# ABOVE the catch-all. The anchor is left intact (not self-consuming; E-005 N/A).
# Order relative to the is_binary clause is irrelevant: `:{{.error-code}}` is an
# atom, is_binary only matches binaries — disjoint patterns.
#
# Idempotency is the engine's implicit planted-MARK guard: a re-run with the same
# code finds MARK:error-shape-<code> already present and skips. No ASLONG is
# needed, and REANCHOR is deliberately ABSENT — its comma-splice is only correct
# for comma-separated collections (Op A), never for blank-line-separated clauses.
IN "api/lib/barkpark/content/errors.ex"
### Insert build/1 clause for :{{.error-code}} above the catch-all
INSERT AFTER FIRST
::: is_binary internal_error clause :::
  defp build({:error, reason}) when is_binary(reason),
    do: %{code: "internal_error", message: reason, status: 500}
::: is_binary internal_error clause :::
WITH
::: {{.error-code}} build clause :::

  # scaffy:add-error-shape {{.error-code}} MARK:error-shape-{{.error-code}}
  defp build({:error, :{{.error-code}}}),
    do: %{code: "{{.error-code}}", message: "{{.Message}}", status: {{.Status}}}
::: {{.error-code}} build clause :::
MARK "error-shape-{{.error-code}}"

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# OP C — the unit test (envelope shape + known_codes/0 membership tripwire)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# errors_test.exs is a flat test list (no describe blocks) closed by the module
# `end` at :290. Tests are separated by BLANK LINES, so — like Op B — this is an
# INSERT AFTER FIRST, anchored on the last test (the label_spine membership
# tripwire, :287-289, unique). The new test is inserted after it, before the
# module `end`. Idempotency is the implicit planted-MARK guard; no ASLONG, no
# REANCHOR (blank-line-separated, not comma-separated).
#
# The new test asserts BOTH the envelope (code/message/status) AND
# MapSet.member? on known_codes/0 — the deliberate tripwire, because the OpenAPI
# drift-guard is a tautology (known_codes derives from @hints): drop the @hints
# entry Op A planted and this membership assertion is what fails.
IN "api/test/barkpark/content/errors_test.exs"
### Insert a {{.error-code}} test after the label_spine test
INSERT AFTER FIRST
::: label_spine test block :::
  test "label_spine is a registered code (OpenAPI enum + hint table truthful)" do
    assert MapSet.member?(Errors.known_codes(), "label_spine")
  end
::: label_spine test block :::
WITH
::: {{.error-code}} test :::

  # scaffy:add-error-shape {{.error-code}} MARK:error-test-{{.error-code}}
  test "maps :{{.error-code}} to its envelope and registers {{.error-code}} in known_codes" do
    Logger.metadata(request_id: nil)

    env = Errors.to_envelope({:error, :{{.error-code}}})
    assert env.code == "{{.error-code}}"
    assert env.status == {{.Status}}
    assert env.message == "{{.Message}}"
    # additive fix-suggesting hint, like every other registered code
    assert is_binary(env.hint) and env.hint != ""
    # the deliberate tripwire: known_codes derives from @hints, so this membership
    # assertion is what catches a dropped @hints entry (the OpenAPI guard can't).
    assert MapSet.member?(Errors.known_codes(), "{{.error-code}}")
  end
::: {{.error-code}} test :::
MARK "error-test-{{.error-code}}"

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSTCONDITIONS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# ASSERT FILE: each op's mark is present (verbatim substrings the ops write).
ASSERT FILE "api/lib/barkpark/content/errors.ex" CONTAINS "MARK:error-hint-{{.error-code}}"
ASSERT FILE "api/lib/barkpark/content/errors.ex" CONTAINS "MARK:error-shape-{{.error-code}}"
ASSERT FILE "api/test/barkpark/content/errors_test.exs" CONTAINS "MARK:error-test-{{.error-code}}"

# ASSERT CMD: the errors unit test (envelope shape + membership tripwire) AND the
# served-vocabulary coverage guard. Scoped single-file `mix test` is LOCAL-safe
# with a warm api/_build (charter A2, RESOLVED 2026-07-16: this exact pair runs
# 27 tests green in ~0.7s warm) — no DB (both are `use ExUnit.Case`), no phx.server.
# NOTE: errors_doc_coverage_test.exs (the §9 ratchet) is deliberately NOT asserted
# here — see the §9 manual-step note below; a build/1-only code cannot satisfy it
# until §9 is hand-edited.
ASSERT CMD "cd api && CC=/usr/bin/clang mix test test/barkpark/content/errors_test.exs test/barkpark_web/contract/error_code_coverage_test.exs"

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# §9 — the ONE required MANUAL step (why it is not an op)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# docs/api-v1.md §9 lists the public error vocabulary in human prose, and
# api/test/barkpark/content/errors_doc_coverage_test.exs is the anti-drift RATCHET:
# it asserts every known_codes/0 code appears verbatim in backticks in §9. So
# after this command runs, add a line for {{.error-code}} to §9 by hand:
#
#     `{{.error-code}}` {{.Status}} — {{.Message}}
#
# placed in the category that fits (additive vs. endpoint-specific), TRIMMING
# adjacent prose to stay within the 14000-byte budget (check-doc-budgets.sh, an
# enforced merge gate — api-v1.md currently has ~9 bytes of headroom, and the doc

# What this plants, and why it is ONE INSERT BEFORE FIRST (D58 → W6 ratify)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A canonical marker is two comment lines that must sit DIRECTLY ABOVE a public
# entry point, because scripts/docs-anchors-check.sh §8(b) asserts a public
# `def `/`func `/`export ` within 6 lines BELOW every `@canonical capability:`
# line. The only byte-exact, line-granular anchor for "directly above the head"
# is the head line ITSELF — so the op is INSERT BEFORE FIRST anchored on the
# head: the payload (provenance line + @canonical line) splices above it and
# the head survives UNTOUCHED as a pure anchor.
#
# HISTORY (why this op used to be a REPLACE): before INSERT BEFORE was ratified
# (D55 deferral), prepend-above-a-surviving-head was only expressible as a
# self-consuming REPLACE re-emitting the head, and E-005 then FORCED a REANCHOR
# alongside the payload-derived ASLONG. That forced REANCHOR was not merely
# vestigial — it was the corruption vector that ratified this primitive: on a
# SECOND different-slug marker in the SAME file, the per-slug guard doesn't
# skip, the `MARK:canonical-` family match hijacks the anchor, and the splice
# either aborts (tail desync, D33) or comma-mutates the previously marked head
# and plants a duplicate head line — run-proven in the W6 ratify experiment
# (task scaffy-backlog-insert-before-primitive). As a plain INSERT the op is
# not self-consuming, carries no REANCHOR, and a second marker in the same
# file is an independent clean insert.
#
# Idempotency: the planted `MARK:canonical-{{.slug}}` is the implicit re-run
# guard (a plain MARK skips when already planted), and the payload-derived
# ASLONG below is the explicit belt to that suspender.
#
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# PRE-RUN CHECK — the different-slug double-mark residual (D58)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The ASLONG guard is per-SLUG (`capability:{{.slug}}`). It refuses a re-plant
# of the SAME slug, but it is BLIND to a DIFFERENT-slug marker already sitting
# on the same head — a run with a fresh slug against an already-marked head
# would cleanly stack a second marker above the same entry point. Before
# running, grep the target for an existing marker on YOUR head:
#
#     grep -n '@canonical capability:' <TargetFile>
#
# If the head already carries a marker, DON'T run this — a public entry point
# owns at most one capability slug. This is the demand-driven doctrine
# (CLAUDE.md "Canonical-impl markers"): tag ONLY a genuinely-forked or
# jargon-named capability that a cold agent would otherwise have to find among
# decoys — a well-named, unforked function earns no marker, and a marker is
# REMOVED once dedup kills its decoys. The marker certifies "one owner," never
# "bug-free."
#
# Token spellings (D3d / A1): every variable here is OPAQUE, so each renders in
# exactly ONE spelling — no casing transforms. `{{.slug}}` is the capability
# name, never a code identifier; `{{.HeadLine}}` / `{{.TargetFile}}` /
# `{{.Aka}}` / `{{.CommentToken}}` are all verbatim literals.

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# OP — splice { provenance + @canonical } directly above the head (W6)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The fenced anchor is the head line, byte-exact and line-granular: INSERT
# BEFORE FIRST splices the payload at the anchor's first occurrence, leaving
# the head bytes untouched. The provenance line plants the real mark
# `MARK:canonical-{{.slug}}` (D24 — a plain MARK requires its `MARK:<name>`
# text in the op's own payload; present here, and it doubles as the implicit
# re-run skip). ASLONG is the @canonical line's own `capability:{{.slug}}`
# substring (payload-derived per E-006; ASCII, brace-free, no `}}` beside a
# literal `}`).
IN "{{.TargetFile}}"
### Plant @canonical capability:{{.slug}} above the marked head
INSERT BEFORE FIRST
::: target head line :::
{{.HeadLine}}
::: target head line :::
WITH
::: {{.slug}} canonical marker :::
{{.CommentToken}} scaffy:add-canonical-marker {{.slug}} MARK:canonical-{{.slug}}
{{.CommentToken}} @canonical capability:{{.slug}} aka:{{.Aka}}
::: {{.slug}} canonical marker :::
MARK "canonical-{{.slug}}"
ASLONG FILE DONT CONTAIN "capability:{{.slug}}"

# POSTCONDITIONS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# ASSERT FILE: both planted lines are present. Both strings are verbatim
# substrings the op writes and are guard-consistent with the ASLONG (A4/A5:
# ASCII, no `}}` adjacent to a literal `}`).

ASSERT FILE "{{.TargetFile}}" CONTAINS "MARK:canonical-{{.slug}}"

# PUBLIC entry point, i.e. a `def `/`func `/`export ` within 6 lines below the
# `@canonical capability:` line. `grep -A6` scopes to exactly the §8 window; this
# is the cheap, litter-immune local proof that the marker is well-placed.

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# THE ENSURE LAW (charter D57) — why this is not a MARK-guarded command
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# An ensure command guarantees a line a developer could just as well have typed
# by hand. So idempotency keys on that HAND-REPRODUCIBLE line — the full import
# text `import {{.Module}}` — and NEVER on a `MARK:` comment. This is the whole
# distinction from add-oban-worker / add-cli-verb, whose guards key on the mark:
# there, scaffy OWNS the block it plants. Here it does not — a human import and a
# scaffy import are the same line, and the guard must treat them identically.
#
# Two consequences fall out of that law, both binding on every ensure-* command:
#
#   1. A NO-OP RUN WRITES NO RECEIPT. If the guard already sees `import {{.Module}}`
#      (however it got there — scaffy earlier, or a hand edit), the op is skipped
#      and NOTHING is written: no file change, and crucially no receipt in
#      `.scaffy/receipts/`. Scaffy records only what it actually did.
#
#   2. `bp scaffy remove` AFTER A SKIP EXITS 4 — AND THAT IS CORRECT. remove is
#      receipt replay (D36). A skipped ensure wrote no receipt, so remove finds
#      none and exits 4 (ReceiptMissingError), leaving the file untouched. Scaffy
#      never owned that import line, so it must not remove it. Exit 4 here is the
#      SUCCESS signal of the ensure contract, not a failure — do not "fix" it.
#
# SUBSTRING FALSE-SKIP CAVEAT (read before using on submodule imports). The guard
# is a plain substring test: `import {{.Module}}`. So `import Logger` is a
# substring of an ALREADY-PRESENT `import Logger.Handlers` — the run would skip
# and never add the bare `import Logger` you asked for. The guard cannot tell a
# prefix apart from a whole import. Mitigation: pass the EXACT module you mean; if
# you need `import Logger` and the file already imports `import Logger.Handlers`,
# the two are genuinely different imports and this substring guard will not add
# the second — insert it by hand, or narrow the design (a trailing-newline guard
# is not expressible in a single-line ASLONG). This is a known, documented edge;
# for the overwhelmingly common flat-module case it is a non-issue.

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# OP — insert `import {{.Module}}` once, directly after the anchor line
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# INSERT AFTER FIRST {{.AnchorLine}}: the payload lands immediately below the
# first occurrence of the caller's anchor. The payload plants a provenance
# comment carrying the mark (so remove has a handle and a reader sees where the
# line came from) plus the import itself. The mark name is the FIXED kebab
# `ensure-import`: a plain MARK requires its `MARK:` text verbatim in the payload
# (it is here), and it need not be per-module unique because remove is receipt
# replay keyed on command+vars (D35/D36) — two ensured imports in one file get
# two receipts and retract independently, even sharing the mark comment.
#
# The ASLONG guard is the ENSURE LAW in one line: DONT CONTAIN the import text
# itself. It is a verbatim substring of the payload (E-006, add polarity → guard
# derives from what the op writes), ASCII, and brace-safe (`}}` is followed by a
# space, never a literal `}`).
IN "{{.TargetFile}}"
### Ensure `import {{.Module}}` exists after the anchor line
INSERT AFTER FIRST
::: anchor line :::
{{.AnchorLine}}
::: anchor line :::
WITH
::: {{.Module}} import :::
  # scaffy:ensure-import {{.Module}} MARK:ensure-import
  import {{.Module}}
::: {{.Module}} import :::
MARK "ensure-import"
ASLONG FILE DONT CONTAIN "import {{.Module}}"

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSTCONDITIONS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The import is present (verbatim substring of the payload the op writes). This
# ASSERT FILE holds whether scaffy inserted the line this run or a prior run / a
# hand edit already had it — the ensure contract guarantees the END STATE.
ASSERT FILE "{{.TargetFile}}" CONTAINS "import {{.Module}}"

# Compile gate — an import of a module that does not exist fails compilation.
# Every Elixir gate is TIER ci (A2): never run in the apply worktree, only on CI
# where the BEAM toolchain is provisioned. A skipped (no-op) run still asserts —
# the end state is what is checked.
ASSERT CMD "cd api && mix compile" TIER ci

# ===========================================================================
# add-backfill-task — the DECLARATIVE form of the byte-identical idiom every
# `barkpark.*.backfill` Mix task hand-copies.
#
# PRIOR ART & EVIDENCE. `api/lib/mix/tasks/` carries a family of one-shot
# backfill tasks — barkpark.edges.backfill, barkpark.media.backfill,
# barkpark.preview.backfill, barkpark.paper.backfill_block_ids,
# barkpark.paper.doctrine_backfill — each independently re-typing the SAME
# safe-by-default skeleton: `use Mix.Task`, `@switches [dry_run:, apply:,
# dataset:]`, the parse-and-raise-on-invalid preamble, and the load-bearing
# negation guard that makes a bare invocation a dry run. The canonical guard
# is `api/lib/mix/tasks/barkpark.edges.backfill.ex:51` — this command mirrors
# that exact expression VERBATIM (it is the payload-derived ASSERT FILE guard
# below), so a task authored here is byte-faithful to the exemplar the whole
# corpus already agrees on.
#
# ALL-CREATE, ZERO INJECTION. Like add-plugin and add-migration, this command
# touches NO accretion file — a Mix task is DISCOVERED, never registered:
# `Mix.Task.load_all/0` walks the `Mix.Tasks.*` module namespace at invocation
# time, so dropping a module under `lib/mix/tasks/` on the `elixirc_paths` tree
# IS the registration. There is no router, barrel, registry, or config map to
# inject into, so every op below is a whole-file `CREATE FILE IF ABSENT` and
# there are zero `MARK` ops (MARK anchors a marker INSIDE a host file; this
# command has no host file). Idempotency and reversibility are therefore
# structural: IF ABSENT is the guard (a second run writes nothing), and the two
# created file paths are the remove handles (Wave-3 `remove` deletes exactly
# this set, leaving the tree byte-clean).
#
# COMPILES AS-IS, MUTATION IS A FENCED TODO. The created task compiles and RUNS
# today: the dry-run path streams the corpus, counts candidate rows, and reports
# — writing nothing. The actual write is a clearly fenced TODO region inside the
# single `unless dry_run?` block, so the safe default can never write and the
# author fills in only the mutation. The four-way flag truth table is factored
# into a PURE `dry_run?/1` so the paired test pins it WITHOUT booting the app or
# touching the DB (LOCAL-safe warm `mix test`, A2's scoped-single-file gate).
# ===========================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1/2 ● Task module — lib/mix/tasks/barkpark.<task>.ex
#     Mirrors barkpark.edges.backfill.ex: the house moduledoc with the "Safe by
#     default" section, @shortdoc, @switches, the parse-and-raise preamble, the
#     byte-exact negation guard (factored into the pure dry_run?/1), and a
#     Repo.stream sweep whose write is a fenced TODO. Lives on the elixirc_paths
#     tree so `mix` discovers it — no registration edit exists to plant.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE FILE IF ABSENT "api/lib/mix/tasks/barkpark.{{.task_name}}.ex"
WITH
::: {{.task_name}} task module :::
defmodule Mix.Tasks.Barkpark.{{.TaskName}} do
  @moduledoc """
  {{.Summary}}

  ## Safe by default

  A bare invocation is a DRY RUN — it streams the target rows, counts the ones
  that still need the backfill, and reports what WOULD change without writing.
  Pass `--apply` to actually perform the mutation.

      # report only (writes nothing) — the safe default
      mix barkpark.{{.task_name}}
      mix barkpark.{{.task_name}} --dry-run

      # perform the backfill
      mix barkpark.{{.task_name}} --apply

      # narrow to one dataset
      mix barkpark.{{.task_name}} --apply --dataset production
  """
  @shortdoc "{{.Summary}}"

  use Mix.Task

  import Ecto.Query, only: [from: 2]

  alias Barkpark.Content.Document
  alias Barkpark.Repo

  @switches [dry_run: :boolean, apply: :boolean, dataset: :string]

  @impl Mix.Task
  def run(args) do
    Mix.Task.run("app.start")

    {opts, _argv, invalid} = OptionParser.parse(args, strict: @switches)

    if invalid != [] do
      Mix.raise("Unknown arguments: #{inspect(invalid)}")
    end

    dry_run? = dry_run?(opts)
    dataset = Keyword.get(opts, :dataset, "production")

    {:ok, {scanned, changed}} =
      Repo.transaction(fn ->
        dataset
        |> base_query()
        |> Repo.stream()
        |> Enum.reduce({0, 0}, fn row, {scanned, changed} ->
          if needs_backfill?(row) do
            unless dry_run? do
              # -- TODO: PERFORM THE MUTATION --------------------------------
              # Replace this block with the real write for `row`, e.g.
              #
              #     row
              #     |> Document.changeset(patch_for(row))
              #     |> Repo.update!()
              #
              # Keep every write INSIDE this `unless dry_run?` so the safe
              # default can never write; the dry-run path already counted it.
              # --------------------------------------------------------------
              :ok
            end

            {scanned + 1, changed + 1}
          else
            {scanned + 1, changed}
          end
        end)
      end)

    Mix.shell().info("scanned #{scanned} row(s) in #{dataset}; #{changed} need backfill")

    if dry_run? do
      Mix.shell().info("\nDry run — nothing was written. Re-run with --apply to write.")
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Safe-default flag logic — write ONLY when `--apply` is explicitly given and
  not negated by `--dry-run`. Any other combination is a dry run. Pure and
  side-effect-free (no app boot, no DB) so it is unit-tested directly. This
  expression is byte-identical to the corpus exemplar
  `barkpark.edges.backfill.ex:51`.
  """
  def dry_run?(opts) do
    not (Keyword.get(opts, :apply, false) and not Keyword.get(opts, :dry_run, false))
  end

  # The rows still awaiting the backfill. Narrow this to the real predicate
  # (a NULL column, a missing content key, a stale version) so the sweep only
  # touches what it must.
  defp base_query(dataset) do
    from(d in Document, where: d.dataset == ^dataset)
  end

  # TODO: return true only for rows that still need the backfill. Left total
  # (false) so a fresh task is a safe no-op until you fill in the predicate.
  defp needs_backfill?(_row), do: false
end

blocks.title: INSERT BEFORE — the deferral that hid a silent-corruption bug

content.value: D55 had deferred INSERT BEFORE as ergonomics: “prepend above a surviving head” was already expressible as a self-consuming REPLACE re-emitting the head, and add-canonical-marker shipped on that idiom. The ratify experiment run-proved the deferral wrong in kind, not degree — the idiom was a latent defect: E-005 forces a REANCHOR family onto every self-consuming REPLACE, and for the prepend idiom that clause is a corruption vector. Marking a second, different-slug capability in the same file left the per-slug guard silent, the planted MARK:canonical- family hijacked the anchor, and the splice either aborted (D33 tail desync — {/do-terminal heads) or silently corrupted under a green report (}-terminal one-liner heads: a comma appended to real code plus a duplicate bodyless head). As a plain INSERT BEFORE FIRST the op is not self-consuming, carries no REANCHOR, and the two-slug scenario is two independent clean inserts — pinned forever by TestCanonicalMarkerTwoSlugsOneFile. Census after the ratify: 1 INSERT BEFORE FIRST, REPLACE 11 → 10; INSERT BEFORE LAST is grammar-legal with zero corpus instances. Stated in the benchmark papers' house style: the deferral was wrong, the experiment said so, the grammar moved.

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# WHY HEAD-INSERT, NOT TAIL-APPEND — the survey ruling, stated honestly
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two idioms compete for a list append:
#
#   * REANCHOR comma-list append (add-cli-verb / add-schema-type): REPLACE the
#     list's LAST element verbatim, re-emit it + comma + the new element. That
#     needs a byte-exact tail anchor — possible only because those commands PIN
#     their target (tickets/cli.ex; the three byte-identical minimal-template
#     plugins). Here the target is VARIABLE and every plugin's tail element is
#     different bytes, so a fenced tail-REPLACE is impossible by construction.
#
#   * Separator-safe bare INSERT (add-sdk-method / the zones): insert after a
#     never-consumed anchor, payload carries its own separator. The ONLY
#     byte-uniform anchor across the six block-list plugins is the function
#     head + list opener — grep-proven exactly once per file, absent from the
#     two other shapes:
#
#         def register_routes(_ctx) do
#           [
#
# The head position is not a compromise — it is the house ordering LAW. Within
# one plugin+bucket, list order IS match order (the macro inlines tuples in
# order; Phoenix takes the first match). History's own route adds moved
# head-ward for exactly this reason: `/tasks/prime` landed above `/tasks/:doc_id`
# with the in-tree comment "prime must mount BEFORE /tasks/:doc_id or it
# resolves as a doc id", and `/tasks/events` followed it citing "the prime
# precedent" (#2509). A NEW STATIC path at the head can never be shadowed by an
# existing dynamic catchall — correct by construction, the common case. The one
# hazard the author owns: a new route whose path carries a DYNAMIC segment
# matches first, so check it does not swallow an existing static sibling under
# the same prefix (the mirror of the check a hand tail-append owes existing
# dynamics — no regression vs hand practice). Sibling accretion: the anchor is
# never consumed (INSERT leaves it intact), so a second run stacks its route
# directly under the opener, ABOVE earlier plants — newest-first, deterministic,
# no REANCHOR family needed (the add-schema-type read-pipeline precedent).
#
# EMPTY-LIST EDGE, cut with evidence: a plugin with no routes spells it
# `def register_routes(_ctx), do: []` (github wave-1, #1229) — a one-liner the
# two-line anchor refuses loud. Hand-open the block-list form first; that
# upgrade IS the moment the plugin grows its first route. No plugin in the tree
# spells an empty multi-line list, so the trailing comma below always has a
# following element to separate.

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# OP — the route tuple, planted at the head of register_routes/1
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Guard = the tuple's method+path head, payload-derived (D3c): method+path IS
# route identity, so a re-run skips clean AND a hand-authored duplicate route
# refuses injection (stronger than guarding the mark line alone). The written
# tuple is one line; if the substituted values push it past the formatter's
# margin, `mix format` wraps it exactly as tickets.ex:265-268 shows — the
# guard's method+path head survives any such wrap.
IN "api/lib/barkpark/plugins/{{.plugin}}.ex"
### Plant the {{.method}} {{.path}} route at the head of register_routes/1
INSERT AFTER FIRST
::: register_routes list opener :::
  def register_routes(_ctx) do
    [
::: register_routes list opener :::
WITH
::: {{.plugin}} {{.method}} route tuple :::
      # scaffy:add-plugin-route {{.plugin}} {{.method}} {{.path}} MARK:plugin-route-{{.plugin}}-{{.method}}-{{.action-name}}
      {:{{.method}}, "{{.path}}", {{.Controller}}, :{{.action_name}}, auth: :{{.auth_bucket}}},
::: {{.plugin}} {{.method}} route tuple :::
MARK "plugin-route-{{.plugin}}-{{.method}}-{{.action-name}}"
ASLONG FILE DONT CONTAIN "{:{{.method}}, \"{{.path}}\""

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSTCONDITIONS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Both grep-shaped closes are verbatim substrings the op writes (A4,
# guard-consistent with the ASLONG). The compile proof is TIER ci (A2: every
# mix gate compiles the world; Elixir suites are not local-safe).
ASSERT FILE "api/lib/barkpark/plugins/{{.plugin}}.ex" CONTAINS "MARK:plugin-route-{{.plugin}}-{{.method}}-{{.action-name}}"
ASSERT FILE "api/lib/barkpark/plugins/{{.plugin}}.ex" CONTAINS "{{.Controller}}, :{{.action_name}}, auth: :{{.auth_bucket}}"
ASSERT CMD "cd api && mix compile" TIER ci

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# OBSERVED: the dev-loop recompile gotcha (not a command step — a footgun map)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Mix cannot see the router's dependency on register_routes/1 (the plugin
# module is reached dynamically through the Registry), so after this op a plain
# `mix compile` recompiles the plugin but NOT the router — the manifest shows
# the change while the route 404s. Force it in dev:
#
#     rm _build/dev/lib/barkpark/ebin/Elixir.BarkparkWeb.Router.beam && mix compile
#
# (router/plugins.ex:100-116 states the law; CI and `make rebuild` compile from
# clean and never hit it.)
